ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs and material trading counterparties against: (i) the Swiss SECO consolidated sanctions list reflecting UN Security Council and EU autonomous measures; (ii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists; (iii) FATF high-risk jurisdiction list; and (iv) the domestic PEP database with adverse-media review, performed prior to notarization of the Articles of Association and prior to opening any Swiss bank account, in accordance with AMLA Art. 6 and FINMA supervisory practice. The Baijiu export relationship is categorized Low_Risk_Standard, but a written AML/CFT risk assessment, the HS 2208.90 customs classification, and full underlying trade documentation for Swift Wire and Letter of Credit payment rails must be archived with the registered agent.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Swiss Central Business Names Index (Zentraler Firmenindex, ZEFIX) at https://www.zefix.ch, administered jointly by the Federal Commercial Registry and the cantonal Commercial Register Offices (Handelsregisterämter)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Art. 950 of the Code of Obligations and Art. 3 HRegV, the company name must be expressed in an official Swiss language (German, French, Italian or Romansh), must not be deceptive and must not offend legitimate public interests. The Chinese brand designation must be transliterated into Latin script in accordance with official romanization rules and must include the legal-form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG'. The proposed name must be clearly distinguishable from all existing ZEFIX entries and must indicate the spirits trade through tokens such as 'Liquor', 'Spirits', 'Baijiu' or 'Distillery' in order to avoid confusion.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a refusal by the cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant must file a formal written objection within 30 days of receipt of the negative decision to the Cantonal Supervisory Authority for the Commercial Register. If the refusal is upheld, a further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court in Saint-Gall within 30 days of the date of the supervisory decision, pursuant to Art. 37–38 HRegV and the Federal Administrative Procedure Act. The rejected name may be replaced at any time by a fresh and distinct reservation filed at ZEFIX, without affecting any other pending incorporation filings.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as the sole registered office. Art. 626 and Art. 977 of the Code of Obligations require the registered seat to correspond to the actual administrative centre of the company. For this Baijiu export wholesale entity, a pure virtual office or postal address is not permitted; a professional domiciliation service or shared business centre is tolerated only where executive management, books and records remain physically accessible in the seat canton and directors can be reached during business hours. Cantonal practice for a non-banking goods exporter requires an identifiable physical location in the seat municipality.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk of less than 5% per annum for a non-banking wholesale exporter; unannounced on-site substance checks are typically triggered by VAT or customs registration, activation of the spirits import/export licence, unusual payment patterns or adverse media, rather than by routine incorporation procedures.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations, arts. 620-659 (Aktiengesellschaft), arts. 633 and 641-652 (capital and shares); Commercial Register Ordinance, arts. 12-23; Alcohol Act, SR 231.1, arts. 2, 10-17 and 49-61; Swiss Civil Code, art. 52.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), operated under the Federal Commercial Register Supervision.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised Articles of Incorporation (Statuten) together with the Commercial Register application (Handelsregisteranmeldung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Share capital must be at least CHF 100,000; at least CHF 50,000 must be actually paid up before registration. The paid-up cash contribution must be blocked in a Swiss bank escrow account, evidenced by a bank blocking confirmation (Sperrerklärung) delivered to the notary and the commercial register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company subscribes to the issued share capital of CHF 100,000, composed of 2,000 registered shares at CHF 50 nominal value each, and that the founder-subscribers' cash contributions be paid into the blocked Swiss bank account as required by art. 633 CO. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is established at [Zug address], Switzerland. RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed: [Name] as Chairperson of the Board, [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] as Secretary (non-board), effective immediately. RESOLVED, that the board is authorised to execute all registration filings before the Cantonal Commercial Register and to retain counsel for corporate, liquor-export and data-protection compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public authorised for the Canton of Zug and licensed Swiss bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Swiss notary to prepare the draft Articles of Incorporation and coordinate the opening of a blocked capital escrow account. Deposit at least CHF 50,000 in cash at the bank; instruct the bank to issue a blocking confirmation addressed to the notary. Confirm the identity, civil capacity and signature samples of each founder and proposed board member.
required_dossiers: Founders' valid passports or equivalent national IDs
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Bank account opening forms for the blocked capital escrow
Signed subscription declaration for each proposed share
Criminal record extract for each proposed board member (when requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the origin of funds, submit the required documentary evidence; if a founder's identity document is incomplete, provide a notarised copy or apostilled translation and request notarial re-operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct the statutory formation meeting before the notary. Record the subscription of all shares, adoption of the Articles, election of the board, designation of authorised signatories and declaration that the minimum paid-up capital has been duly blocked. The notary authenticates the deed and issues the public instrument required for commercial registry filing.
required_dossiers: Draft notarial deed and articles
Bank blocking confirmation (Sperrerklärung)
Written acceptance by each board member
Specimen signatures of officers
Copy of the founders' identities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the share subscription or capital confirmation, correct the articles or subscriptions by supplemental notarial amendment and re-authenticate without reopening the full proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed application for registration with the Handelsregisteramt, either via the Swiss commercial register electronic platform (Zefix/e-shop) or physically, attaching the authenticated formation deed, articles, blocking confirmation, list of board members and statements of consent. Pay the notarial, registration and federal fees. The registry enters the AG into the Commercial Register and publishes the registration in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce.
required_dossiers: Notarial formation deed
Articles of Incorporation
Bank blocking confirmation
Board and managers' written appointments and consents
Authorised signatory specimen signatures
Declaration of no bankruptcy/relevant pending proceedings for officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a due-process query, remedy within the stated statutory deadline by submitting a notarised corrective statement or supplementary authorisation; appeal any refusal within 10 days to the Cantonal Commercial Registry Supervision Authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal tax, VAT and social-insurance registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) and the relevant Zug Canton compensation office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Commercial Register entry, register the AG for VAT through the FTA internet portal; the export of goods is generally zero-rated for Swiss VAT, but registration is mandatory for active wholesale/export operations. Register the employer and employees with the AHV compensation office for social security and accident insurance accounts.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt after entry
List of authorised signatories and company addresses
Board resolution on VAT and payroll registration
De minimis export turnover projection or contract evidence
Company bank account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FTA imposes a penalty for late VAT registration, submit the registration history and request an interest/penalty reduction; for AHV cession, amend the wage declaration and pay outstanding contributions with voluntary interest.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG) – Swiss Alcohol Board, alcohol permit division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for a commercial alcohol operating permit covering wholesale and export of distilled spirits. Provide company details, shareholding, operational plan, storage premises, intended foreign markets and proof of compliance with the Alcohol Act. Upon approval, obtain the permit number and any attached authorisation for temporary customs warehouse storage of exported goods.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt
Company organisational chart and compliance manual
Description of premises and storage arrangements
List of intended export destinations and counterparties
Certificate of no criminal background for the business conduct representative
Tax clearance certificate from the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit missing descriptions and audit-proof evidence of storage segregation; an informal hearing may be held at BAZG; a formal refusal can be appealed to the Federal Administrative Court within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational safety, fire certification and physical storage clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zug Cantonal Labour Inspectorate; municipal fire protection service; and cantonal building authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the office and distribution warehouse as workplaces. Obtain a fire-safety certificate after inspection of fire extinguishers, emergency exits and electrical installations. For areas storing palletised containers of packaged spirits, perform structural load verification and issue a warehouse storage plan if required by the municipal building office. Confirm compliance with occupational maximum workplace concentrations for ethyl alcohol evaporation.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and floor plans for registered premises
Fire protection concept signed by the safety officer
Structural static certificate for racked storage
Valid liability/all-risk insurance certificates
Employee instruction records on manual lifting and ethanol hazards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a fire or structural inspection fails, provide a corrective plan and schedule the re-inspection; for minor non-compliance, pay a rectification fee and file evidence of completion within 20 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swiss Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG) – Swiss Alcohol Board, in coordination with the Zug Cantonal Trade Office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Alcohol Operations Permit (Alkoholhandelsbewilligung) for wholesale and export of distilled spirits

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN), Cantonal Environmental Protection Agency of Zug.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / light notification (Exempt from full EIA) because the activity is limited to trading, warehousing and export distribution of packaged alcoholic beverages; no production, no bulk ethanol handling and no significant plant operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater and packaging waste must comply with the Swiss Water Protection Act (GSchG) arts. 6-10 and the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV); no process VOCs are emitted except minor evaporation from closed containers; any leakage or bursting of bulk containers must be contained within sealed areas and disposed of by an authorised waste operator under the Technical Ordinance on Waste (TVA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification issued by the Zug municipal fire inspection; structural load approval for racked storage; occupational health and safety clearance for employees handling high-proof liquor containers; emergency-response scheme approved by the cantonal labour inspectorate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Federal Tax Administration FTA), Schwarztorstrasse 50, 3003 Bern, Switzerland; official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; electronic filing and VAT registration portal: https://gateway.estv.admin.ch. Federal value added tax is administered exclusively by the ESTV; cantonal and communal tax authorities separately administer cantonal and communal income and capital taxes on entities resident in their territory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity without a Swiss Commercial Register entry that becomes liable for Swiss VAT must register with the ESTV by submitting Form 106 'VAT Registration Request' (also available through the federal EasyGov portal and the ESTV e-service). The application must include proof of identity of the entity, foreign VAT/TIN certificate, identification of the authorised signatory, evidence of Swiss economic activity, and an estimate of expected Swiss taxable turnover. The ESTV then issues a Swiss VAT number (MWST-Nr./No TVA) together with a UID-CH business identifier. For a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG) incorporated in Switzerland, the definitive UID-CH number is allocated automatically by the Commercial Register at incorporation, and VAT registration is completed separately with the ESTV using the recognised Swiss VAT registration process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG) is a distinct taxable corporation subject to federal, cantonal, and communal corporate income and capital taxes on its worldwide net profits, with relief for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate. Switzerland does not grant pass-through or transparency treatment to an AG, and the entity classification is not elective.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss tax law does not recognise US-style check-the-box elections and provides no general hybrid mismatch election. Statutory election mechanisms available under Swiss VAT law include: (i) the optional exercise of VAT liability by a small business whose turnover is below the CHF 100,000 exemption threshold (Art. 21 para. 3 Swiss VAT Act); and (ii) the election to form a VAT group among closely linked entities, allowing group-wide treatment as a single taxable person (Art. 52 Swiss VAT Ordinance). At the corporate income tax level, the participation deduction applies automatically without an election, and no elective transparent treatment exists for an AG.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer, MWST; Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA; Imposta sul valore aggiunto, IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of taxable turnover in Switzerland excluding VAT within a calendar year, in accordance with Art. 10 Swiss VAT Act; small businesses below this threshold are exempt unless they elect to become taxable, and foreign suppliers of certain electronic, digital, or intangible B2C services are subject to registration when their Swiss turnover reaches the same statutory threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance system, official digital stamping regime, or mandatory continuous-control API with the tax authority. Taxpayers are free to issue invoices in paper or electronic format provided the invoice satisfies the content requirements of Art. 26 Swiss VAT Act. Accepted electronic formats include Swiss QR-invoice and standard Swiss e-invoicing formats. Vendors using fiscal or POS systems must ensure data integrity and auditability, but no prior governmental authorisation or clearance of invoices is required. The ESTV performs post-event documentary audits rather than pre-clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Switzerland to a foreign country are zero-rated pursuant to Art. 23 Swiss VAT Act when the goods are physically transported out of Switzerland by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf, the supplier acts in its own name and for its own account, and the export is formally declared to customs. For baijiu exports, the distilled spirits must leave Swiss customs territory under an approved Swiss customs export procedure. The zero-rating also extends to direct domestic supplies to export-oriented purchasers only when the statutory conditions for export are met. The taxable person must retain adequate proof of export to support the zero rate.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration regularly audits export zero-rating claims by inspecting the customs export declaration, transport documents, and payment evidence. If the exporter cannot substantiate the physical export or if the stated export is found to be fictitious, the zero-rated supply is retrospectively recharacterised as a taxable domestic supply, and the VAT is clawed back at the standard rate together with default interest. Intentional tax evasion or fraud in connection with zero-rating claims may attract criminal fines of up to four times the tax evaded, confiscation of the avoided tax, and imprisonment for serious cases; negligent failure to maintain proper export proof may result in monetary penalties and reassessment. Reputational and commercial consequences include exclusion from simplified export procedures and compulsory prepayment of VAT in future periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca nazionale svizzera)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility on both the current and capital account of the balance of payments. The Swiss franc is freely convertible into foreign currencies; there is no exchange-control licensing regime, no central bank approval requirement for inward or outward remittances, and no statutory restriction on profit repatriation. Dividend distributions remain subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax, although treaty-based or EU/FTA relief may reduce this rate if the beneficial owner is eligible. Funds transfers are monitored solely under anti-money-laundering, sanctions, and reporting obligations rather than exchange-control rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists under Swiss law to surrender export proceeds to the Swiss National Bank, to convert export receipts into Swiss francs, or to repatriate them within a prescribed timeline. Exporters may hold, invest, hedge, or redirect export proceeds freely in any currency. Banks, however, must report balance-of-payments data to the Swiss National Bank consistent with the Federal Act on the National Bank and FINMA reporting circulars, and the underlying fact-pattern must still satisfy Swiss anti-money-laundering and trade-compliance documentation standards.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency settlement account and documentary credit account
Operations account, FX risk-management line, and commercial trade finance facility
Core operational account and trade settlement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury and liquidity-clearing use. Switzerland does not recognise EU/UK-style electronic-money institution passports; a foreign EMI licence does not authorise holding Swiss customer accounts or conducting payment business in Switzerland. FINMA banks under the FinTech regime may accept public deposits up to CHF 100 million under a special licence, but such entities are not equivalent to full clearing banks and cannot issue or negotiate documentary credits. Offshore digital EMIs should be treated as auxiliary payment channels only, never as the legal settlement rail for capital escrow, FX execution, or import/export trade finance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss anti-money-laundering law does not mandate a physical interview for every foreign corporate client; FINMA-recognised video identification may satisfy identification duties if the bank implements a compliant remote-identification procedure. In practice, most tier-1 Swiss banks still require a physical or video-notarised interview with natural-person directors and ultimate beneficial owners before opening settlement accounts for a newly formed Aktiengesellschaft, particularly where the shareholder is non-resident and the commercial activity is export trading. The CH_AG should therefore plan for at least a director meeting with the onboarding account officer and provide notarised corporate attestations; remote-only opening is possible but not a reliable standard assumption.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial-ownership chain combined with non-resident individual shareholders connected to jurisdictions with stricter outward capital controls.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss official extract of the commercial register, notarised register of beneficial owners, passport and proof of residence of every natural-person UBO, tax residence certificate, source-of-wealth declaration backed by bank statements, board resolution appointing the Swiss director and bank signatories, audited opening balance sheet or capital-payment evidence, and a reference letter from the corporate service provider that formed the AG.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering indicators in spirits wholesale: invoice over- or under-valuation, blending/miscounted products, or excise-duty sensitivity on high-proof alcoholic beverages.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial framework agreement, per-shipment sales contracts, pro-forma invoices, packing lists, order confirmations, customs export/import declarations from both Switzerland and destination country, certificates of analysis, certificates of origin, full set of shipped bills of lading, cargo insurance certificates, warehouse receipts, excise-tax payment evidence, and contemporaneous treasury/payment reconciliation records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, embargo, or export-control red flags if the buyer network touches SECO, EU, UK, or OFAC-listed entities, or if end-uses become opaque in a transshipment structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions screening logs for all counterparties, adverse-media search reports, end-user and end-use attestations, country-specific embargo checks, ICC compliance attestation from the distributor, beneficial-ownership evidence for every buyer, and a protective compliance manual containing escalation procedures to the Swiss Secretariat for Economic Affairs.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital for CH_AG should be remitted by SWIFT wire transfer using the MT103 format with a unique end-to-end transaction reference. The ISO 20022 purpose code should identify the payment as a capital injection, preferably 'CAPC' for capital contribution, with the narrative field stating 'Inward direct investment – equity contribution to Swiss Aktiengesellschaft'. The remitting shareholder should transmit from the company’s disclosed bank account, attach the notarised share subscription resolution and capital-confirmation certificate, and the receiving Swiss bank must verify the sender’s beneficial-owner details and the underlying corporate resolution. No Swiss National Bank conversion or licensing approval is required, but the receiving bank will report the transaction for balance-of-payments statistics. If the remitter is in China, the remittance must also satisfy the People’s Bank of China/SAFE outward-remittance review including a verified foreign direct investment filing, otherwise the transfer may be blocked at source.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to suppliers, distilleries, and logistics providers should run as SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers, preferably with SWIFT gpi tracking, from the CH_AG’s validated operational account. For supplier financing and documentary transactions, the bank should issue an import letter of credit via link:true MT700 with UCP600 attachment, using MT707 for amendments, and settle against presentation of commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, insurance certificate, certificate of origin, and conformity certificates as required. Domestic Swiss franc leg payments may be cleared through the Swiss Interbank Clearing system (SIC / SIC4 if applicable); euro payments can be routed via SEPA-compatible rails, while US-dollar commercial payables should remain on the SWIFT correspondent banking network using MT103/MT202 cover conventions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts in USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, and CNH/CHF
Offshore CNY non-deliverable forwards (CNY NDF) as a lawful hedge for non-convertible CNY exposure
FX swaps between CHF and EUR or USD for treasury liquidity steering
Cross-currency swaps to match long-term liabilities and funding currency
Vanilla FX options (call-spread and put-spread structures) for asymmetric trade-receivable protection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements and discharge of the Board of Directors at the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders (statutory corporate body); approved statements retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of closing of the financial year (Art. 699 para. 2 Swiss Code of Obligations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court may convene the AGM upon shareholder request at company cost; directors personally liable for damage; failure to constitute statutory organs triggers Commercial Register strike-off procedure (Art. 731b CO)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and cantonal corporate income tax return with signed annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration of the registered office and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deadline set by the tax canton, commonly 6 to 8 months after financial year end (calendar-year AG: usually 31 March to 30 April following the tax year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% p.a. on outstanding tax, late-filing surcharge up to 25% of assessed tax, and criminal penalties for intentional non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value Added Tax settlement (quarterly or annual VAT return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each VAT reporting period; annual filing available where authorized by FTA for a 12-month reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at statutory rate (currently 4%-5% p.a.) plus administrative penalty up to the amount of the tax evaded; seizure and penalty proceedings for repeated defaults

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual verification and integrity confirmation of the Register of Members and Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory register maintained at the registered office; subject to inspection by Commercial Register authorities, tax administration and AML supervisors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous updating upon each share transfer; annual board confirmation of accuracy alongside the AGM preparation cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directorial criminal liability and administrative fines under Art. 697m CO for knowingly false or incomplete UBO entries; disqualification consequences for missing shareholder records

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Spirits export compliance: excise exemption certification and annual spirit stock/trade statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Customs Administration (FOCBS/BAZG) and Federal Alcohol Administration (EAV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Per-shipment customs export declarations; annual reconciliation of tax-exempt spirit movements filed with the competent customs office by 31 January following the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Customs administrative penalty and default interest; revocation of trade authorization; forfeiture of goods for unsubstantiated exemption claims

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) statutory audit required when two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: total balance sheet CHF 20 million, net sales CHF 40 million, annual average 250 full-time employees (Art. 727 CO). Smaller AGs are subject to a limited audit (Art. 727a CO) unless they have fewer than 10 full-time employees and unanimous shareholder consent resolves full audit waiver (opting-out).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss accounting law per Art. 958b ff. CO; Swiss GAAP FER for medium, large and parent entities; IFRS permitted for listed companies and comparable issuers; small companies may apply simplified presentation per Art. 960 ff. CO.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The register of beneficial owners (Art. 697j-697m CO) is a mandatory internal register; entries must be created upon share acquisition, updated in case of ownership changes, and verified annually by a board resolution. No routine central UBO filing is currently due for a standard private AG; the register must be disclosed to the tax authority, the enforcement office and financial intermediaries upon request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes of Board of Directors' Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal Direct Federal Tax (approximately 7.83% on a pre-federal-tax basis); combined cantonal and communal corporate income tax rate varies by seat, approximately 11.9% to 21.1%, with illustrative Zug combined rate of 11.9%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays for trading or wholesale distribution companies. Available reliefs include the participation exemption for qualifying intercorporate dividends and capital gains, the cantonal/federal IP license box regime and R&D super-deduction where qualifying IP and Swiss R&D activities exist. Export trading profits from Chinese Baijiu wholesale distribution are taxed as ordinary commercial income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal legal entity tax return (Geschäftssteuererklärung / Déclaration fiscale pour les personnes morales) consolidated with the Direct Federal Tax assessment; filed electronically via the competent cantonal tax administration's secure e-filing portal and the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (SFTA) eTax / ePortal channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; provisional federal and cantonal corporate income tax payments are made quarterly on account and are not separate filing returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year (for a 31 December year-end, generally by 30 June of the following year), unless the cantonal tax authority grants an extension, commonly until 30 September. The Direct Federal Tax assessment is lodged together with the cantonal return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name and seat, Swiss UID / CHE number, legal form (Aktiengesellschaft / AG), registered share capital, board members, registered shareholders, industry code ISIC 4632 and Swiss alcohol/spirits export distribution licence reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Swiss UID, foreign tax identification numbers and country of tax residence for all non-resident shareholders; attach articles of association, register of shareholders and beneficial ownership details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Swiss statutory balance sheet and income statement in CHF, including export sales, cost of goods sold, warehousing, logistics, commissions and distribution expenses in accordance with the Swiss Code of Obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File Swiss statutory accounts, signed audit report if required, and reconciliation from origin-country GAAP to Swiss GAAP; convert all foreign-currency amounts at the year-end exchange rate and disclose Chinese Baijiu inventory pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses and deduction of tax-free income; adjustments for hidden profit distributions, excessive management fees, non-arm's-length royalties, representation costs and depreciation differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all related-party transactions with Chinese and other non-resident entities; add back excessive intercompany charges and interest; support deductions with contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of carried-forward tax losses within the seven-year period; claims for participation exemption, IP license box deductions and other statutory capital or business reliefs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Evidence legal and economic substance for relief claims; non-resident-controlled companies must document actual Swiss decision-making, staff and functions; attach loss carryforward schedules and supporting ownership certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Taxable Capital and Withholding Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable net profit and taxable paid-in capital for cantonal capital tax; reconciliation of Swiss anticipatory tax account on dividends paid and received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report dividends distributed or credited to non-resident shareholders; confirm statutory 35% withholding tax or treaty-reduced rate; attach anticipatory tax return/refund forms and foreign tax residency certificates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers administrative orderly fines up to CHF 10,000, cantonal reminder fees, default surcharges and late-payment interest of approximately 4.5%-5%. If books are not produced, the tax authority assesses ex officio. Intentional misconduct triggers evasion penalties of up to three times the evaded tax and criminal fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss anticipatory/withholding tax on gross cash and in-kind dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss payer must withhold 35% at source. A non-resident shareholder claiming China-Switzerland DTA relief must obtain a Chinese Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and file a refund/relief application with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration using the official Swiss withholding tax claim/refund form within the statutory period, generally three years from payment. The applicant must prove beneficial ownership and, for the 5% treaty dividend rate, direct shareholding of at least 25% for at least 365 days. Treaty relief is subject to anti-abuse, economic substance and principal-purpose review.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss domestic law imposes no withholding tax on ordinary arm's-length royalties or commercial loan interest. Interest on Swiss bonds and money-market instruments remains subject to 35% anticipatory tax. Under the China-Switzerland DTA, interest and royalties may be taxed in the source state at a maximum of 10%, but because Swiss domestic source taxation is 0% for ordinary royalties and interest, no Swiss withholding tax is collected. Payments recharacterized as constructive dividends are subject to 35% anticipatory tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed Swiss statutory Local File/Master File threshold; all material related-party transactions must be demonstrably arm's length when challenged. Mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least CHF 900,000,000. Swiss audit practice expects contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for high-risk cross-border flows involving Chinese Baijiu procurement, licensing, financing and distribution.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations. However, Swiss corporate residence requires statutory seat and effective management; treaty benefits and withholding tax relief require genuine economic substance such as physical office, employees, bank accounts, board meetings and business risk control. Letterbox companies with nominee directors and centralized management abroad risk denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization, withdrawal of tax rulings and retroactive assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional submission of materially false tax returns; omission of Baijiu export revenues or commissions; fabricated supplier invoices; undisclosed foreign bank accounts or payment rails; double bookkeeping; destruction of accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative evasion surcharge of up to three times the evaded tax; orderly fine up to CHF 10,000; criminal fine and imprisonment of up to three years for tax fraud; default interest; retroactive assessment and loss of tax-preferred treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false returns or order concealment face criminal prosecution, imprisonment, personal restitution obligations to the tax authority, travel bans, passport seizure, asset freezing and board disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to Chinese or other non-resident shareholders without withholding the statutory 35% anticipatory tax; disguising dividends as management fees, royalties, commissions or shareholder loans; failure to pay over withheld amounts to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The distributing company is liable for the unwithheld 35% tax, plus default interest, procedural fines and an evasion surcharge of up to three times the evaded tax; unpaid anticipatory tax is a preferential claim in insolvency proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members who approve or participate in non-compliant distributions are personally liable for unpaid withholding tax; criminal sanctions include imprisonment, confiscation, travel bans and monetary restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Hidden Profit Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length purchase prices paid to related Chinese Baijiu suppliers; excessive distribution or management service fees to non-resident affiliates; interest-free shareholder loans; artificial routing through Hong Kong or crypto payment intermediaries; absence of contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss tax authorities recharacterize excess payments as constructive dividends subject to 35% withholding tax and additional Swiss corporate income tax; expenses are disallowed; default interest, evasion penalties and transfer pricing audit referrals apply; double economic taxation may result.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize unfair related-party transactions breach fiduciary duties under Article 754 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; they may face civil restitution actions, personal bankruptcy liability, criminal penalties, travel bans and director disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Treaty Shopping and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Swiss AG maintained as a letterbox with no office, staff, Swiss bank account or Swiss board meetings; management decisively exercised from China; claim of treaty benefits or participation exemption without beneficial ownership; use of nominee directors and artificial financing structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of China-Switzerland DTA withholding tax relief; recharacterization of Swiss tax residence; retroactive taxation of Swiss-source profits; cancellation of favourable tax rulings; forced liquidation under Swiss company law; negative registration with Swiss authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors risk criminal liability for aiding tax evasion, false attestation and money laundering; courts may impose travel bans, asset seizures, personal liability for unpaid taxes and prohibition from serving as Swiss directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Trade Sanctions and Customs Misdeclaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting undocumented cash, crypto or third-party payments in the Baijiu export trade; dealing with sanctioned jurisdictions or persons; false customs declarations; undervaluation or overvaluation of exported goods; failure to report suspicious transactions to the Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions under Articles 305bis and 305ter of the Swiss Criminal Code, including fines of up to three times the laundered value and imprisonment; customs and excise penalties up to five times evaded duties; confiscation of goods and proceeds; suspension or revocation of the Swiss spirit export licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for failing to implement adequate AML controls and for wilful participation in unlawful conduct; penalties include imprisonment, personal asset confiscation, travel bans, reputational destruction and permanent exclusion from Swiss management roles.
